cover.title: Customer Goal Attainment: Data Source Map
cover.subtitle: Which tables answer 'what % of our customers hit their goal?'
takeaways: A live report already answers this ('Campaign Groups Hitting Goal Percentage', Mode, runs daily): ~63% of active campaign groups hitting goal on 2026-07-20 (Upper Mid 71%, Mid 66%, SMB 58%).
Goals are stored, not guessed: bae.v_daily_goal_by_campaign_group gives each group's goal_type + goal_value per day; compare to actual performance from the summary facts.
Before quoting it: CostPerCompletedView auto-passes (~25% of goals), the grain is campaign-group not advertiser, and it's a trailing-3-day status; those are the refinements.

sheets.name: Table map
sheets.finding: MNTN already stores each customer's goal; these tables let you score it
sheets.method: Grouped by role: the goal, the customer, what they achieved, reach, incrementality, and how the numbers are computed. Top two rows are the ready-made goal spine the existing report uses. Full BQ paths; join keys in the last two columns.

rows.What's in it: Authoritative as-of-day goal per campaign group: goal_type_id + goal_value + goal_type_name, one row per group per day. Prefer over live campaign_groups.goal_value when you need the goal as it stood on a date.
Maps each campaign group to the targeting feature it had active (feature_type = KW / PP / KW+PP) over [start_date, end_date). Lets you cut goal attainment by AUDI feature.
Where the goal actually lives: goal_type_id (which metric) + goal_value (the target number) + budget + objective_id, one row per campaign group.
Decodes goal_type_id into the goal metric + plain-English definition. 16 types: ROAS, eCPA, CPA, CostPerVisit, VisitRate, Visits, Efficiency (reach), CTR, etc.
Objective enum (Prospecting, Retargeting, etc.) - the campaign's intent, separate from its numeric goal.
The recommended media plan + deliverability_classification (high/med/low delivery risk) - signals whether the goal was even reachable.
Advertiser master dim: company_name (authoritative), active/deleted/is_test flags, attribution windows, control_group_percentage.
Maps campaign -> campaign_group -> advertiser; carries funnel_level, objective_id, channel_id (8=CTV, 1=display).
Advertiser -> industry vertical (parent + sub-vertical) - used to benchmark 'good' against peer verticals.
PRIMARY scoreboard: daily spend, visits (views+clicks), conversions, order value at campaign-GROUP grain - the exact grain goals are set at.
Same KPIs rolled up to the whole advertiser account - answers 'the advertiser as a whole'.
Campaign-grain daily KPIs; history back to 2024 - best table for long trends / pre-periods.
Wide combined fact (spend+visits+conversions+impressions+reach) that powers the client-facing UI via CHAPI - the number customers actually see.
The four component fact tables at fresh hourly grain - use these when the daily rollups lag (~2 weeks).
Households / users reached (HLL sketch) at group grain - for reach / awareness goals. Merge the HLL, never SUM it.
Ghost-bid holdout lift: treatment vs holdout visits/conversions per advertiser & campaign group - success beyond attribution. Rollup is pre-aggregated.
rows.Grain: 1 / day x adv x cg x campaign x ip x arm

rows.What's in it: reporting_style = industry_standard vs last_touch - decides WHICH visit/conversion columns count toward the goal. Archive gives as-of-date history.
Media cost at event grain - the spend denominator behind ROAS/CPA/CPV when you need it below daily grain.

sheets.name: Already built
sheets.intro: A live report already answers this question end to end; start there.
blocks: A report already does this

A Mode report, 'Campaign Groups Hitting Goal Percentage' (app.mode.com/mntn/reports/30fb4d3f8447), runs daily and answers this directly. For each active campaign group it scores trailing-3-day performance against the as-of goal in bae.v_daily_goal_by_campaign_group and reports the daily % hitting goal, split by advertiser spend tier and by targeting feature. Reuse its logic before building anything new.
What it reads today (2026-07-20)

About 63% of active campaign groups are hitting goal: Upper Mid Market 71%, Mid Market 66%, SMB 58% (larger advertisers hit goal more often). By feature: KW 57%, KW+PP 58%, PP 56%. Tiers are advertiser monthly spend: SMB under $25k, Mid Market $25-65k, Upper Mid Market $65k+.
How it decides 'hit'

ROAS (goal_type 1): order_value / spend, hit if >= goal. CostPerVisit (13) and CPA (16): spend / visits or / conversions, hit if <= goal. CostPerCompletedView (14): hit is hard-coded to 1. Active = trailing-3-day spend >= $100. Visits / conversions / revenue include competing_* (first-touch), i.e. industry_standard attribution for everyone.
Caveats before quoting the number (where we can add value)

- CostPerCompletedView auto-passes regardless of performance and is ~25% of all campaign groups with a goal, which inflates the headline; strip or properly score it for a true rate. - It is campaign-GROUP grain; 'what % of customers' needs a roll-up to advertiser. - 'Hitting goal' is a trailing-3-day live status, not a whole-flight outcome. - Attribution is industry_standard for all, not each advertiser's reporting_style. - Four goal types are scored, but they cover ~95% of groups that have a goal (only Efficiency / reach is dropped).

sheets.name: Join map
sheets.intro: How the tables connect - the appropriate join column, table by table.
blocks: The spine: three keys

Almost every join runs on three columns. advertiser_id is the account. campaign_group_id is the GOAL grain - the goal (goal_type_id + goal_value) is set on the campaign group, so this is the key you attribute success at. campaign_id rolls up to campaign_group_id via integrationprod.campaigns (campaign_id is the PK -> campaign_group_id -> advertiser_id). Everything else hangs off these three.
Decoding the goal

campaign_groups.goal_type_id -> silver.core.goal_types.goal_type_id turns the code into the metric name + definition (16 types). campaign_groups.goal_value is the target number, expressed in the units of that metric (goal_type CostPerVisit -> a $ per visit; ROAS -> a multiple; VisitRate -> a percentage). campaign_groups already denormalizes goal_type_name, so you only need the join when you also want the description. objective_id -> silver.core.objectives separates prospecting vs retargeting intent.
Joining the goal to the result

The cleanest attainment join is campaign_groups -> sum_by_campaign_group_by_day on campaign_group_id (plus a date filter on day), because both sit at campaign-group grain. For the whole-account view, roll to sum_by_advertiser_by_day on advertiser_id. For long trends use sum_by_campaign_by_day on campaign_id, then map campaign_id -> campaigns.campaign_group_id. all_facts and the four *_facts tables share the same 19 dimension keys (advertiser_id, campaign_group_id, campaign_id, channel, objective, ..., hour) - join any of them on the subset you need.
Reach and incrementality

Reach: sum_by_campaign_group_by_hour on campaign_group_id - its user-count columns are HLL sketches, so use HLL_COUNT.MERGE, never SUM. Incrementality: lift__ghost_bid_visits on advertiser_id / campaign_group_id / campaign_id (arm = 'ghost' = holdout vs 'submitted' = treatment); the pre-rolled gold.reporting.lift__ghost_bid_rollup is already per advertiser & campaign_group.
The column that changes the answer

r2_advertiser_settings.reporting_style (join on advertiser_id) is industry_standard vs last_touch, and it decides WHICH visit/conversion columns count. Under industry_standard the client UI = the default columns + competing_* (first-touch); under last_touch it drops competing_*. Resolve this per advertiser before scoring, or two analysts get two different 'did they hit it' answers. Field-level history for as-of-date resolution is in archives_advertiser_setting_archives.
Naming and hygiene gotchas

For a current advertiser name always join integrationprod.advertisers.company_name - advertiser_verticals.advertiser_name is write-once and ~80% empty for recent accounts. On every integrationprod dim, filter deleted = FALSE AND is_test = FALSE.

sheets.name: How to answer it
sheets.intro: A recipe for turning these tables into the percentage the request asks for.
blocks: Recipe: campaign (group) level

1) Pull the as-of goal per group per day from bae.v_daily_goal_by_campaign_group (goal_type_id + goal_value). 2) From sum_by_campaign_by_day (or _group_by_day) over the window, compute the ACTUAL value of that same metric (ROAS = order_value / spend; CostPerVisit = spend / visits; VisitRate = visits / impressions; CPA = spend / conversions), deciding whether to apply competing_* / reporting_style. 3) met = actual beats goal_value in the right direction (>= for ROAS / VisitRate / Visits; <= for the cost / CPA goals). 4) % = met / (campaign groups that have a goal set). This is exactly what the existing Mode report does on a trailing-3-day window; see the 'Already built' tab.
Recipe: advertiser level

Roll the same logic to sum_by_advertiser_by_day, or define account-level 'goal met' as e.g. >= X% of the advertiser's campaign groups hitting their goal. The request is answerable at either grain; pick which one up front, because the percentages differ.
Watch-outs

- goal_value can be null or 0 (no goal set): exclude or bucket those separately. - Low-impression weeks give extreme rates; filter weeks under ~1,000 impressions. - The daily rollups lag ~2 weeks; for the latest window read the *_facts tables directly. - 'Met the goal' here is attribution-based; ghost-bid lift answers the harder 'was it incremental'.
If the ask needs to be richer later

Goals as set today are a single metric per campaign group. A blended 'success' score (performance + reach + incrementality together) is a scoring model built on top of these tables, not a column that already exists; treat that as a follow-up, not part of this pull.
